title: Al-Sharaa Announces Specific Ministerial and Gubernatorial Appointments in First Post-Assad Reshuffle
detail: Syrian transitional President Ahmad al-Sharaa announced detailed ministerial and gubernatorial appointments in Syria's first cabinet reshuffle since Assad's ouster. In a significant nepotism-optics move, al-Sharaa removed his brother Maher al-Sharaa as Secretary-General of the Presidency, replacing him with former Homs Governor Abdul Rahman Badreddine al-Aama. New ministers appointed included Khaled Fawaz Zaarour as Information Minister and Basel al-Suweydan as Agriculture Minister. New provincial governors were named for four key governorates: Ghassan Elias (Quneitra), Murhaf Khaled al-Naasan (Homs), Ahmed Ali Mustafa (Latakia), and Ziad Fawaz al-Ayesh (Deir ez-Zor). The reshuffle came amid public protests over economic conditions and international pressure for broader governance reforms. Al Jazeera reported the reshuffle as a consolidation milestone for the al-Sharaa administration as it works to stabilize governance and address Western concerns about the transitional process.

media.caption: Syria's first cabinet reshuffle since Assad's fall brings new ministers and governors
